We’d never say the films should be redone or changed - but we can certainly wish for another reality in which some of the deleted scenes were added in. But what is done cannot be undone - luckily they still gave us a behind the scenes look into what could’ve been.
It’s a shame really that some of us still haven’t seen some of the alternatives that could’ve been - but we hope we can solve that problem with our in-depth look into some of the best deleted scenes. So sit back and hold onto your wands - it’s gonna be a bumpy ride.

snippet.title: Uncharted Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
Video game lovers, movies lovers, fans of Tom Holland - this is the movie for you! After about a decade of planning, the adventure movie following Nathan Drake is here and the process to make it a reality was far from easy. Before even getting off its feet, the movie went through seven different directors! 
One of the best parts of the film is the special bromance between Mark Wahlberg and Tom Holland - but just because they liked each other didn’t mean they were easy on their co-stars! Holland doubled down on his work, training like a machine in the five-month break when the production was shut down because of the pandemic. The actor gained a huge amount of muscle mass so he didn’t look like such a kid next to the intensely buff Wahlberg.
Training wasn’t all he did - Holland got to work mixing drinks behind a real bar to practice his moves for the film so he could really flair and bartend. On the set he took it one step further - Holland was making drinks with real alcohol in them and was sending them out to different crew members. The party didn’t stop when they wrapped - Holland managed to pull off a spontaneous Friday night party right on set!
It wasn’t all fun and games - the stunts in this movie left Holland seriously battered and bruised - and with tendinitis in a hamstring. The injuries and toll it took on his body were so intense that the actor had to ask for a weekend off so he could rest! 
Why do all the stunts look so good? Probably because they were shot practically and Holland got as close as a person actually can to tumbling out of an airplane safely! This is just the tip of the iceberg of all the work and planning that went into bringing Uncharted to the big screen but luckily, all of it paid off.

snippet.title: Zendaya Shares Painful Experience Playing Rue In Euphoria

Is there a single episode of Euphoria that doesn't have some kind of intense and dramatic through line? Not at all and this made working through it all an extra challenge for the actors, especially Zendaya who goes to incredibly dark places and violent places. Going from being known as the Disney kid to a daring, dramatic actor portraying a drug addict was quite the jump, but it’s one the actress made effortlessly. While she was able to pull out the performance, Zendaya was pretty intimidated, wanting to make sure her performance lived up to expectations.
The content discussed and portrayed in Euphoria is intense- so living through it at work each day while already struggling with general anxiety made the work days tricky, but worth it in the end luckily. As if working all those hours weren’t exhausting enough, spending hours crying or going through something painful on a completely whacked-out schedule is downright impossible - but Z’s schedule demanded it.
It wasn’t easy, but the support of an amazing cast and crew made playing Rue a safe and secure experience. Zendaya goes through the pain for the cameras, but behind the scenes, all the people around her on set are usually feeling the emotions with her and shedding tears.
It’s a major challenge, but Zendaya has risen to the occasion - she didn't earn that Emmy for nothing! Thank goodness for a trustworthy and supportive team that can help to make it all possible.

David Bradly’s charming personality is really lost in his performance. And Timothy Spall played a rat in human form. Or a human in rat form. snippet.title: 15 Actors Who Took Things TOO Far For A Role
snippet.description:
The speculations surrounding method acting are always the most extreme examples - and usually they’re the ones always making the headlines. We’re going into some of the most extreme examples and some where it was questionable as to why the actors went as far as they did for the role. We never imagined that some of these instances would take such disgusting turns.
Of course there are repeat offenders on this list - like Robert Pattinson and Jared Leto. But the outcomes of their performances cannot be matched. However, they could’ve gone about it another way that doesn’t end up endangering themselves. Even some of our favorite superheroes jumped on the extreme method acting game. You never know what actors will do to take on a heavy role. The work really does make a difference, but we cannot help but wonder - was it really necessary? And what if they were never able to break out of these strange habits and lifestyles?
We’ve always wondered what it takes to produce these powerful Oscar worthy performances and how it ends up affecting the actors. It can sometimes get carried away and negatively impact the rest of the cast and crew. Once it gets too far - the mental and physical aspects of the actor can self-destruct. They always have to be cognizant of the fact that the work they put in - will inevitably produce either good or bad consequences. We’ll let you decide which ones went a little too far.

The place they shot wasn’t a building at all. The team went ahead and built a four-story, hundred-foot wall to work its magic - and it worked!

snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors Being The Opposite Of Their Characters
snippet.description:
The actors in the Harry Potter films were good - there’s no question about it. Taking a look behind the scenes and in their interviews proves just HOW good they are - sometimes being the total opposite of the characters they played. For some of the more evil characters, this was a pretty good thing. We never thought we’d find any part of Voldemort charming, but when Ralph Fiennes is being himself, he is a pretty solid guy! He had no problem getting into character when it was time to shoot, but when the cameras weren’t rolling, there was a much nicer vibe around him.
Emma Watson is a lot like Hermione, but not in some key ways! The actress was actually getting fined for being unprofessional on set - Watson got a few red cards filming. snippet.title: Marvel Series Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
It wouldn’t be a Marvel show if there wasn’t a whole lot of magic behind the scenes to bring all that we see ON screen to life. We’re covering some of the coolest stunts, CGI, costumes, and tiny details that went into Loki, WandaVision, The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, and Hawkeye.
When Loki dropped into the TVA - he was LITERALLY dropped. When Lady Loki actress Sophia needed a costume that allowed for taking care of some mom duties - a costume director with a creative mind and knack for zippers took care of the issue. When the time came to fight, Tom Hiddleston didn’t hold back, performing a ton of hand-to-hand combat himself!
WandaVision took advantage of a lot of tech - but not just from this decade! Throwing it back to the ’50s, the whole team traveled back in time. Vision looked a bit different on set for a few reasons - the main being the fact that he was a whole lot more blue than usual! Agatha Harkness was brought to life by Kathryn Hahn, but all the magic came with the help of a village of a crew and some heavy-duty fans.
Hawkeye brought a very special character to life in the MCU - Lucky the Pizza dog, played by Jolt the golden retriever. While Yelena’s blip used loads of complex CGI - the environments were shockingly all real - requiring a ton of extra work and precision for the team.
Bucky Barnes thought his arm was his own - until he discovered the Wakandan’s could disable it. The arm turned out to have several versions from a cool rubber sleeve to a built 3D model!
If they could dream it, they could do it - and Marvel did not disappoint.

snippet.title: Tom Felton Behind The Scenes Of Harry Potter

We’re taking a deep dive into Tom Felton’s experience on Harry Potter as the villainous role of Draco Malfoy. You're going to be surprised to know he was nothing like that. Tom was graced with the role by complete chance and if it weren’t for his quick-witted thinking, we may not have been able to see him in the titular role. It also helped that he kept character through multiple injuries on set and by just being that older brother figure to many of the younger cast. Felton was pretty unknown of the calibour of the films he was doing, but maybe that was a good thing. If some people had it their way, we would’ve seen a dramatic change in his character later on, but that will never be. His performance lent a hand to the star-studded cast performance and helped us through Draco’s dramatic change in the later films.

The Harry Potter series touched our hearts and helped shape many of our childhoods. Tom Felton was a part of that, making us believe he was the most evil and vile character in the series. Deep down, he is the complete opposite of his on-screen character. He became the Dark Lord’s chosen one and was given the chance to prove his acting chops.

snippet.title: The Voices Behind Disney's Encanto
snippet.description:
We’re heading to Colombia to hang out with one of the coolest families around - none other than the magical Madrigals! This incredible cast is stacked with some of the best performers around - but the secret behind this cast is… many of them never actually acted before! From the seasoned veterans to the newbies who brought their talents to the Disney screen - no one missed a beat when filming Encanto.
Stephanie Beatriz is no stranger to the business - the Argentinian-born actress has spent loads of time doing voiceover in the booth and acting in Brooklyn 99 as Rosa Diaz. Being part of this film was extra special for the actress - especially since her father is Colombian! 
There was no shortage of legends in this cast. We’re talking about the likes of John Leguizamo, María Cecilia Botero, Diane Guerrero, and Wilmer Valderrama just to name a few!
There were some other pros in this movie who didn’t happen to be so well-versed in the filming world - but that didn’t stop them from blowing us out of the water. You’d never guess that Adassa and Mauro Castillo had never done any acting before because their parts in the movie made their mark. We wouldn’t be surprised if we start hearing their voices a whole lot more!
What was extra special about this whole cast is that all of them had some personal connection to Colombia - either they were from there themselves - María Cecilia Botero recorded the entire movie from her home country- or one of their parents was Colombian. Getting to celebrate that culture and passion boosted everyone’s performance and left us with work that is nothing short of amazing. We’re Encanto fans, there’s no doubt about it.

snippet.title: Ozark Actors Least Favorite Scenes To Film
snippet.description:
Ozark is heading into seasons 4 which will be its last. With that, we thought we’d take a look at the least favorite scenes actors had to film. Turns out, there’s quite a few. Expect Julia Garner to appear on the list more than anyone else. While she loves the show and won an Emmy for her role, like a ‘true artist’ she suffered for her art. That could be said of the whole cast. It’s such a dark plot that there was a lot of deep emotion for them to explore. Some actors had to work hard to get into the right mindset and stay there, like Carson Holmes. Others had to work hard at getting themselves out of it, like Julia Garner and Tom Pelphrey. And the mood could sometimes take weeks after filming to shake. Garner’s fear of rodents had her petrified to do a scene with a mouse. While Jant McTeer was adamant she be the one to do her own waterboarding scene for three hours! How did she manage? Nelson Bonilla was heartbroken to not be able to dig into the depths of his character’s monologue while Tom Pelphrey only needed four shots to do his intense scene in the cab and blew everybody’s mind with it. Freezing cold water was a struggle for Michael Mosely. Handling weapons wasn’t the easiest of times for Julia Garner. Accents are an incredible amount of work too. You need it engrained before it’ll work for you. And the ripping out toenails scene left Jason Bateman injured in a way you might not expect. There’s a lot to not like about filming but the cast still love each other and the show. So much so, that Bateman is sad every time a character doesn’t return. Check it out!

snippet.title: 10 Most Painful Scenes To Film In Euphoria
snippet.description:
Euphoria is a tough but amazing watch - and the filming experience for the actors behind the scenes was pretty similar! Whether it was rough emotional scenes that needed to be done, improvised scenes with no hold barred, or complex technical challenges - this team faced it all and they pulled off some amazing feats.
The Carnival scene is one that threw many of the Euphoria fam through the wringer. It looks like one continuous shot, but the trick is - the whole sequence was filmed over six days! This made for long days for the actors who also happened to have to deal with not-so-great weather conditions. One actor actually wound up needing an inhaler just to get through!
Improvising intense scenes means intense emotions might totally overtake an actor! One of the most powerful scenes in the whole series was made up on the spot and really shook everyone involved. Even director Sam Levinson had to walk away and take a breather before continuing with work. Does anyone remember watching Sydney Sweeney in the bathroom? Her moving performance sold the scene, but she wasn’t doing much acting - the actress was really shaken by the end of it.
Jacob Elordi is tough as nails on the show, but in reality, he believes his character is just struggling a lot - and he absolutely is! Elordi is far from the mean character he portrays, which makes being cruel to his co-stars extra tough, really taking a toll on the performer. As for the fights he takes part in? Well, let’s just say duking it out with Few was far from comfortable.
No matter what they had to overcome or how hard it may have been to film some of these moments, in the end, pretty well everyone agrees it was all worth it to tell the story. They’ve got us hooked!
